questions.explanation: After one-quarter turn, velocity directions differ by 90°, so |Δv|=10sqrt2 m/s. Time=8/4=2 s. Average acceleration magnitude=5sqrt2 m/s².

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: Two equal-mass objects move in separate circles with radii r and 4r. If their angular speeds are ω and ω/2, what is the ratio of their centripetal forces F₁/F₂?
questions.explanation: Centripetal force mω²r. F₁=mω²r and F₂=m(ω/2)²(4r)=mω²r, so ratio is 1:1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: A point moves in a circle of radius 0.8 m with centripetal acceleration 5π² m/s². Find its time period.
questions.explanation: a_c=4π²r/T², so T²=(4π²×0.8)/(5π²)=0.64, giving T=0.8 s.

questions.subject: physics
questions.topic: Average velocity versus speed on circle
questions.prompt: A particle completes three quarters of a circle of radius 14 m in 6 s at constant speed. Find the ratio of the magnitude of average velocity to average speed.
questions.explanation: Displacement magnitude between endpoints separated by 90° is 14sqrt2 m. Distance=3/4×2π×14=21π m. Ratio=14sqrt2/(21π)=2sqrt2/(3π).

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: A projectile is launched from level ground with initial speed 20 m/s and reaches its highest point 1.2 s later. If g=10 m/s², what is the horizontal component of its initial velocity?
questions.explanation: At the top, 0=u_y−gt, so u_y=10×1.2=12 m/s. Then u_x=sqrt(u²−u_y²)=sqrt(400−144)=16 m/s.

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: A projectile is launched from ground at 25 m/s and returns to the launch height after 3 s (g=10 m/s²). How far horizontally does it travel during the LAST 1 second of its flight?
questions.explanation: T=2u_y/g gives u_y=15 m/s. Since u=25, horizontal speed u_x=sqrt(625−225)=20 m/s. Horizontal speed is constant, so travel in the final second is 20 m.

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: Two vectors of unequal magnitudes have resultant 13 when aligned and 5 when opposite. If they are then placed perpendicular, what is the resultant magnitude?
questions.explanation: Let magnitudes a>b. From a+b=13 and a−b=5, get a=9,b=4. Perpendicular resultant sqrt(a²+b²)=sqrt(81+16)=sqrt97.
